The script will automatically back up the current asar. After it finishes, just restart opencode. It supports version 1.18.30. Note: You need to run it again after each opencode update. > > [](https://private-user-images.githubusercontent.com/47207976/651074665-314dfc1f-2fd1-4583-b4c5-3a6959806131.png?jwt=eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9..eakjGGMn5ob7RbNZ-H8V78ZjzJ-VLQrYk_IMZUD0-T4) > ## script > > generated by ai > > > Copy and save it as a .ps1 file, then run it. > > $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop" > > # Wait for a key press so the console window does not close before the result is visible. > function Wait-Key { > Write-Host "" > Write-Host "Press any key to exit ..." > [void][Console]::ReadKey($true) > } > > # ---------- Step 0: locate app.asar ---------- > Write-Host "[1/8] Resolve app.asar path from the folder you provide ..." > $inputPath = Read-Host "Enter the opencode install folder" > $inputPath = $inputPath.Trim().Trim('"', "'") > > if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($inputPath)) { > Write-Host "Error: path cannot be empty." > Wait-Key > exit 1 > } > > if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $inputPath -PathType Container)) { > Write-Host "Error: folder not found: $inputPath" > Wait-Key > exit 1 > } > > # 只接受文件夹：优先找其下的 resources\app.asar，其次文件夹内直接存在的 app.asar > $item = Get-Item -LiteralPath $inputPath > $candidates = @( > (Join-Path $item.FullName "resources\app.asar"), > (Join-Path $item.FullName "app.asar") > ) > $AsarPath = $null > foreach ($candidate in $candidates) { > if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $candidate -PathType Leaf) { > $AsarPath = $candidate > break > } > } > if (-not $AsarPath) { > Write-Host "Error: no app.asar found under: $($item.FullName)" > Write-Host "Expected at 'resources\app.asar' or 'app.asar'." > Wait-Key > exit 1 > } > Write-Host " app.asar: $AsarPath" > > # ---------- S

Same setup here (`rtk` plugin + `permission.bash` rules), and I'd add one more consequence beyond the rules not matching: every `gh *`/`git push *` rule has to be duplicated as `rtk gh *`/`rtk git push *`, and the duplication silently goes stale whenever the rewriter changes what it wraps.

Working around it inside the plugin isn't an option for me either, because the rewrite should stay visible in the recorded command (you may want to rerun a rewritten command for its full output), so the fix really has to be on the matching side: evaluate against the pre-hook command, or add a post-permission hook. At v1.18.30 the only hook after `ask()` is `shell.env` (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v1.18.30/packages/opencode/src/tool/shell.ts#L417-L421), which can't touch the command.

The "always" arity fallback to `rtk *` mentioned above makes this worse: one "always" approves every `rtk` command.

Related:
- #34329 and #47674 would let a plugin re-check on its own, but neither exposes the original command.

One more use case for this gate: regex-style bash guardrails from a plugin. Today an allow returns before any plugin can intervene (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v1.18.30/packages/opencode/src/permission/index.ts#L84), and `permission.ask` is never called (#47674), so a plugin can only fail a tool call from `tool.execute.before`, never turn it into a prompt. With a gate, something like `gh api .*--method (POST|PUT|PATCH|DELETE)` → ask becomes a small plugin instead of a fork. It would also help with #35882 if the gate received the pre-hook command. Happy to test a build.

Adding a data point from a different GPU vendor - this is not AMD-specific. Same symptom on Intel UHD + NVIDIA RTX A1000 (Windows 11, VBS/HVCI enabled), app **1.18.30** (auto-updated from 1.18.29, which worked):

**Symptoms**
- App never opens. The main process dies right after `spawning sidecar` in `main.log`; no `utility.log`/`window.log` is ever created; `renderer` never starts.
- 5 Crashpad dumps in 5 minutes (one per launch attempt), ~34 MB each.
- Pure CLI (`opencode serve`) on the same machine works fine - it is only the Electron desktop app.

**Workaround that fully fixes it**
Launching `OpenCode.exe --no-sandbox` starts the app completely: `awaiting server ready` ... `server ready`, window opens, GPU acceleration stays on (gpu-process + renderer alive). No other change needed.

This matches the VBS/HVCI + Chromium sandbox theory in #46691 (the exit code is `STATUS_BREAKPOINT`; the GPU is a red herring). Creating a shortcut with `--no-sandbox` is enough on this machine - no asar repack needed.

Suggest the team consider appending `--no-sandbox` (or a sandbox-compatible launch fix) for affected Windows builds, or detecting the crash loop and retrying with the flag.

Workaround: downgrade to 1.18.29 via Homebrew

Confirmed this resolves the crash. Full steps:

``` bash
brew tap sst/tap
brew trust sst/tap
brew tap-new local/tap
brew extract --version=1.18.29 sst/tap/opencode local/tap
brew uninstall opencode
brew install opencode@1.18.29
brew pin opencode@1.18.29
```

To revert once a fix ships in a newer release:

```bash
brew unpin opencode@1.18.29
brew uninstall opencode@1.18.29
brew install sst/tap/opencode
```

Thanks for the thorough review. All findings have been addressed in the latest push:

**Must fix:**
1. **8 git-internal files** — removed from the tree. Added local excludes in .git/info/exclude to prevent re-adding.
2. **Stale resumeSessionID** — now cleared immediately after auto-resume so a subsequent reload without a sessionID won't reuse the old one.
3. **prepareExecution wiping active/blockers** — removed the force-clear. Only the tui-bootstrap blocker is added; active and existing blockers are preserved.
4. **Title/scope mismatch** — retitled to 'feat(opencode): add reload_config agent tool with auto-resume' since no TUI slash command is registered.

**Should fix:**
5. **store.reload failure** — added failExecution helper that resets reloadInFlight, clears blockers, clears reloadInput/resumeSessionID, and emits a Done event so clients recover instead of deadlocking.
6. **onBusy ordering** — moved yield* onBusy after Deferred.make in runner.ts so a throwing onBusy doesn't leave the session stuck in active.
7. **states Map growth** — completed entries are now pruned from the states Map in continueOrDone when no longer blocked, pending, or in-flight.

**Additional fix found during review:**
8. **store.reload never called on immediate reload path** — request() called prepareExecution but never invoked store.reload. The actual reload only happened on the deferred path via executePending. Now both paths call store.reload after prepareExecution.
9. **Circular import** — ConfigReload.node in LayerNode deps caused a ReferenceError at module load time due to run-state -> config/reload -> session/prompt -> run-state cycle. Removed ConfigReload.node from LayerNode deps in run-state.ts and registry.ts (the service is yielded at runtime via ConfigReload.Service).
